title: Circulating DNA for treatment and follow-up in squamous cell cancers
summary:
A large number of patients with malignant tumors of the head and neck tract (such as oropharynx and hypopharynx), esophagus, cervix and anus have a squamous cell carcinoma (SCC). In these diseases, it is important to detect a progression under therapy or after completion of therapy at an early time point. However, the possibilities of imaging diagnostics are limited and cannot indicate changes that do not yet cause tumor growth. 
There is also a lack of reliable methods to distinguish patients requiring more intensive therapy from low-risk patients. 
Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) can be detected in blood samples of patients with low tumor burden and represents a reliable and prognostically relevant marker for minimal residual disease after curative treatment of different cancers.  
The aim of this study is to show that in patients with squamous cell carcinoma, therapy monitoring by measuring ctDNA in a blood sample can improve patient-specific treatment decisions and detect recurrences at an early time point.


The aim of the present SSC study is 
1)	To investigate the pre-treatment prognostic value of ctDNA measurement 
2)	To confirm the ctDNA elimination pattern during chemoradiotherapy
3)	To establish the role of ctDNA as marker of minimal residual disease and early detection of recurrences
4)	To investigate ctDNA for monitoring during pallative systemic therapies
conditions: Malignant neoplasm, without specification of site

interventions.name:
prospective observational clinical study

At defined time points before, during and after completion of therapy, ctDNA will be measured from the blood of the patient.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Histopathologically verified SCC
Eligible for curatively or palliatively intended treatment
≥ 18 of years
Written and oral consent
Exclusion criteria:
Other cancer disease within 5 year of SCC diagnosis
Conditions that will contraindicate blood samples
Potential lack of compliance to standard FU program and study participation.
